name: Obsidian Gate

stars.name: Obsidian Gate Pulsar
stars.notes: Rapidly rotating neutron star, 14ms pulse period, powerful magnetic field bathes system in periodic radiation

planets.name: Scoria
planets.notes: Radiation-blasted cinder world, surface minerals fused into glass by pulsar beams

planets.name: Basalt Throne
planets.notes: Deep underground settlements shielded from radiation, population 2.4 million miners and researchers

planets.name: Pallid Reach
planets.notes: Massive dead world with unusually strong magnetic field that deflects pulsar wind, creating a sheltered shadow cone

planets.name: Drift
planets.notes: Frozen methane and nitrogen surface, exotic ice crystalline structures sculpted by periodic radiation pulses

anomalies.name: The Toll
anomalies.notes: Extreme gravitational gradient causes frame-dragging effects, ships must calculate precise approach vectors or risk tidal destruction

anomalies.name: Deadlight Corridor
anomalies.location: Aligned with pulsar beam axis, sweeping through orbits 1-3
anomalies.notes: The pulsar's focused beam creates a rotating corridor of lethal radiation; all navigation must account for its 14ms sweep period

asteroid_belts.name: The Shattered Halo
asteroid_belts.notes: Remnants of a world destroyed during the supernova that birthed the pulsar, rich in heavy elements and exotic isotopes

stations.name: Umbra Station
stations.notes: Astrophysics research outpost studying pulsar dynamics, heavily shielded, operates on rotating crew cycles

stations.name: The Crucible
stations.notes: Extraction facility for rare isotopes created during supernova, extremely hazardous working conditions

faction_control.notes: Consortium holds extraction rights but the Terran Science Directorate claims the system should be a protected research zone; tensions escalate periodically

history: Detected in 2291 during a deep-space pulsar survey, the system was initially cataloged as scientifically interesting but commercially worthless due to extreme radiation.
In 2534, prospectors discovered that the Shattered Halo contained supernova-forged isotopes used in advanced drive manufacturing, sparking a hazardous mining rush.
The ongoing jurisdictional dispute between the Veylan Mining Consortium and the Terran Science Directorate has twice escalated to armed standoffs, most recently in 2681.
description: Obsidian Gate is a graveyard and a goldmine in equal measure. The system's neutron star spins fourteen times per second, sweeping twin beams of hard radiation through a court of dead and dying worlds. Everything here exists in the shadow of a catastrophe—the supernova that collapsed the original star left behind a pulsar so energetic that unshielded electronics fail within seconds of direct exposure. The four surviving planets orbit in eerie silence, their surfaces sculpted by forces that would annihilate any unprotected visitor.

Despite the lethality, Obsidian Gate draws people willing to risk everything. The Shattered Halo asteroid belt contains isotopes found nowhere else in the sector—supernova-forged elements critical to advanced propulsion systems. The Veylan Mining Consortium has invested heavily in shielded extraction operations, while the underground warrens of Basalt Throne house the miners, engineers, and support staff who keep the operation running. Meanwhile, Umbra Station's small crew of astrophysicists studies the pulsar itself, publishing papers that have rewritten textbooks on neutron star magnetospheres.

The system's real danger may not be the pulsar but the politics. Two powerful organizations claim authority here, and neither shows signs of yielding. Ships entering the system must declare allegiance or risk being turned away by one faction or the other. Rumors persist of a third interest—unaffiliated scavengers who've found something in the deeper reaches of the Shattered Halo that neither the Consortium nor the Directorate knows about. What they've found, and what they intend to do with it, remains one of the Abyssal Frontier's more troubling open questions.
